extracted.intended_audience: IPPS hospitals, hospital finance staff, Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), and hospital administrators responsible for wage index data submissions and appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and technical standards for constructing the FY 2027 IPPS hospital wage index, including which wage data are included/excluded, formulas for computing salaries/hours/overhead, deadlines and processes for hospitals and MACs to request or contest data corrections, and CMS' authority to make corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of hospital-based RHC and FQHC wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude the salaries, hours, and wage-related costs of hospital-based rural health clinics (RHCs) and Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) from the wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medicare pays for these costs outside of the IPPS (68 FR 45395).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of CAH and REH wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude salaries, hours, and wage-related costs of Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) and Rural Emergency Hospitals (REHs) from the wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAHs were removed because of their substantial negative impact on area wage indexes; any hospital designated as a CAH or REH by 7 days prior to publication of the preliminary wage index PUF is excluded from the calculation. References: FY 2004 and FY 2025 IPPS rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of other wage-related costs (FY2020+)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2020 and subsequent years, other wage-related costs reported on Worksheet S-3, Part II, Line 18 and Worksheet S-3, Part IV, Line 25 and subscripts, as well as all other wage-related costs such as contract labor costs, are excluded from the calculation of the wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As discussed in the FY 2019 IPPS/LTCH final rule (83 FR 41365-41369).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data period used for FY 2027 wage index
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Worksheet S-3, Parts II, III and IV Medicare cost report data for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2022, and before October 1, 2023 (termed 'FY 2023 cost report' or 'FY 2023 data').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data file includes FY 2023 data submitted as of January 21, 2026. Instructions located in Provider Reimbursement Manual (PRM), Part 2, Chapter 40, Sections 4005.2–4005.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of hospitals that terminated participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include wage data for facilities that were IPPS hospitals in FY 2023 (including those that have since terminated participation as hospitals) provided their data did not fail reasonableness edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including these data reflects labor market conditions during the relevant past period and helps ensure the current wage index represents labor market area's current wages versus the national average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and handling of aberrant data
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS identifies and excludes providers with aberrant data from the wage index; excluded providers may be included in the final wage index if data elements are corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027, 68 providers were identified and excluded; certain aberrant data were adjusted and included (for example, imputation where hospitals lacked documentable salaries). MACs instructed to transmit changes by March 21, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of imputation for missing documentable salaries/hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a hospital did not have documentable salaries, wages, and hours for certain services (e.g., housekeeping and dietary), CMS may impute estimates in accordance with policies established in the FY 2015 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imputed estimates follow previously established policies (79 FR 49965–49967).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multicampus hospital wage allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Allot wages and hours for a multicampus hospital among different labor market areas using campus full-time equivalent (FTE) percentages as finalized in the FY 2012 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 includes separate wage data for campuses; CCN subordinate campus identifier placement changed to third position ('B' or 'C') to uniquely identify subcampuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary PUF and hospital review obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Post preliminary, unaudited Worksheet S-3 wage data files and occupational mix files on CMS website; hospitals required to review and, if requesting changes to the May 23, 2025 preliminary files, submit corrections with complete supporting documentation to MACs by September 2, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MACs inform hospitals of availability and processes; hospitals notified via letters from MACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAC transmission and revised PUF schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: MACs were required to transmit revised wage index and occupational mix data to CMS by November 14, 2025, and CMS published wage index PUFs including hospitals' revised data on January 30, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals then had an opportunity to request corrections for CMS or MAC mishandling or to revise adjustments included in the Jan 30, 2026 PUF by February 17, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: February 17, 2026 deadline for hospital correction requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals had until February 17, 2026 to submit requests to MACs to correct errors in the January 30, 2026 PUF due to CMS or MAC mishandling of the wage index data, or to revise adjustments included in the Jan 30 PUF, with sufficient supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data not corrected by this deadline are not considered for correction at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAC transmission of additional revisions (March 20, 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewing hospitals' requested changes, MACs were required to transmit any additional revisions resulting from hospitals' reconsideration requests to CMS by March 20, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS could then make changes and notify hospitals prior to the April deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for CMS intervention requests (April 3, 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline for a hospital to request CMS intervention when the hospital disagrees with a MAC's handling of wage data (including policy, factual, or other disputes) is April 3, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also the deadline to dispute data corrections made by CMS that were notified after Jan 30, 2026 and at least 14 calendar days prior to April 3, 2026 (i.e., by March 20, 2026). Requests and supporting documentation must be received by CMS (and copy to MAC) by April 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final PUF release and limited post-final correction window
rubrics_metrics.description: Final wage index data PUFs planned for posting on April 30, 2026; after the April 2026 PUFs, changes can only be made in very limited circumstances involving an error by the MAC or CMS that the hospital could not have known about before its review of the final PUFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals must notify both MAC and CMS and provide supporting information by May 29, 2026 to be considered for incorporation into the final FY 2027 wage index.

rubrics_metrics.name: May 29, 2026 deadline for notifying CMS/MAC of final-PUF entry/tabulation errors
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after the April 2026 final PUFs, a hospital believes its wage or occupational mix data are incorrect due to MAC or CMS error in entry/tabulation, the hospital must send its request with supporting info to CMS and MAC so it is received no later than May 29, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May 29, 2026 is also the deadline for hospitals to dispute CMS data corrections notified on or after March 21, 2026 and at least 14 days prior to May 29, 2026 (i.e., May 15, 2026). Corrections notified on or after May 16, 2026 may be appealed to the PRRB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural-deadline bar on later challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals that do not meet specified procedural deadlines (e.g., requests to MACs by February deadline and requests for CMS intervention by April deadline) will not be afforded a later opportunity to submit wage index data corrections or to dispute CMS/MAC decisions, including before the PRRB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy finalized in FY 2018 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule and applies to disputes about CMS-initiated corrections as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for midyear corrections (§412.64(k)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Make midyear corrections to the wage index for an area only if a hospital shows that (1) the MAC or CMS made an error in tabulating its data; and (2) the requesting hospital could not have known about the error or did not have an opportunity to correct the error before the beginning of the fiscal year (i.e., by the May deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision is not available to a hospital seeking to revise another hospital's data. If a midyear correction changes the wage index value for an area, the revised value is effective prospectively from the date the correction is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for retroactive correction to beginning of fiscal year (§412.64(k)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A change to the wage index can be made retroactive to the beginning of the Federal fiscal year only when CMS determines all the following: (1) the MAC or CMS made an error in tabulating data used for the wage index; (2) the hospital knew about the error and requested correction using established process and schedule before the beginning of the fiscal year (by the May deadline); and (3) CMS agreed before October 1 that the error was made and the wage index should be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactive correction cannot be used to correct prior years' wage index data; applies only to the current fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS authority under section 1886(d)(3)(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS has authority to make corrections to hospital wage index and occupational mix data to ensure wage index accuracy, as the Secretary must adjust the proportion of hospitals' costs attributable to wages to reflect relative hospital wage levels compared to the national average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS interprets this statutory provision as permitting discretion to make corrections to ensure wages reflect relative hospital wage levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS multistep 15-month review process
rubrics_metrics.description: A multistep, 15-month review and correction process exists for hospital wage data used to create the IPPS wage index for the upcoming fiscal year, including CMS review and potential requests for additional documentation or adjustments from hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although MAC desk review was not performed for FY 2027, CMS conducts regional and national-level analyses to identify additional edits; CMS may discover and correct errors even after posting the January 30 PUF.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS neutrality in correcting errors (direction-agnostic)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS corrects errors to hospital wage data as appropriate regardless of whether the correction will raise or lower a hospital's average hourly wage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: incorporation of positive adjustments from prior-year appeals could increase a hospital's average hourly wage if previously unincorporated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to request review of CMS-initiated corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals are able to request further review of a correction made by CMS that did not arise from a hospital's request, under the timeline/process described in the FY 2018 rule and the FY 2027 Hospital Wage Index Development Timetable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process promotes transparency when CMS makes corrections after the January 30 PUF and allows hospitals to seek review in time for final wage index calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 — Hospital data inclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather data from each non-Federal, short-term, acute care hospital reported on Worksheet S-3, Parts II and III for the hospital's cost reporting period relevant to the wage index. Include hospitals with cost reporting periods beginning prior to Oct 1, 2022 and extending into FY2023 if no other data available. If a hospital had more than one cost reporting period beginning in FY2023, include only the longer; if equal length, include the later period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules determine which cost reporting period's wages/hours are used when multiple periods exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 — Net Salaries formula and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a 'revised' Line 1 by adding Worksheet S-3 Part II Lines 28, 33, and 35 to Line 1, then compute Net Salaries by subtracting GME and CRNA costs (Lines 2, 4.01, 7, 7.01), Part B salaries (Lines 3, 5, 6), home office salaries (Line 8), salaries on Lines 9 and 10 (SNF/home health/other subprovider components not subject to IPPS), and salaries with no hours from the revised Line 1. Net Salaries formula: ((Line 1 + Line 28 + Line 33 + Line 35) − (Line 2 + Line 3 + Line 4.01 + Line 5 + Line 6 + Line 7 + Line 7.01 + Line 8 + Line 9 + Line 10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the initial step in computing a hospital's average hourly wage; terminology changed from 'average' to 'net' salaries in FY 2012 rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 — Total Salaries plus Wage-Related Costs formula and line inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Total Salaries plus Wage-Related Costs is Net Salaries plus contract labor costs for direct patient care and specified services (Lines 11–13), home office salaries and wage-related costs (Lines 14.01, 14.02, 15.01, 15.02), and nonexcluded area wage-related costs (Lines 17, 22, 25.50, 25.51, 25.52). Contract labor and home office salaries without corresponding hours are not included. Wage-related costs for nonteaching physician Part A employees (Line 22) are excluded if no corresponding salaries are reported on Line 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027, include Lines 15, 15.01, and 15.02 in the calculation; propose to use 15.01 and 15.02 instead of Line 15 for future years. Hospitals that reported on Line 15 instead of the split lines will have Line 15 used for FY 2027 to minimize disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 — Total Hours computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Total Hours (Worksheet S-3 Part II) using the same methods as salaries (excluding wage-related costs which have no associated hours): ((Line 1 + Line 28 + Line 33 + Line 35) − (Lines 2, 3, 4.01, 5, 6, 7, 7.01, 8, 9, 10)) + (Line 11 + Line 12 + Line 13 + Line 14.01 + Line 14.02 + Line 15 + Line 15.01 + Line 15.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027 include Lines 15, 15.01 and 15.02; future years to use 15.01 and 15.02 instead of Line 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 4 — Allocation of overhead to excluded areas
rubrics_metrics.description: For hospitals reporting overhead salaries and hours > 0, compute an 'excluded rate' (ratio of excluded area hours to Revised Total Hours) and allocate overhead salaries/hours to excluded areas by multiplying that ratio by total overhead salaries/hours (Lines 26–43). Compute an 'overhead rate' as ratio of overhead hours (Lines 26–43 minus Lines 28, 33, 35) to revised hours excluding contract labor and excluded areas; compute overhead wage-related costs by multiplying overhead hours ratio by wage-related costs (Part II Lines 17, 22, 25.50, 25.51, 25.52) and then multiply by the excluded area hours ratio. Subtract computed overhead salaries, wage-related costs, and hours associated with excluded areas from totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overhead contract labor (Lines 28, 33, 35) excluded from overhead rate determination because hospitals typically do not provide fringe benefits to contract personnel. If hospitals contribute to wage-related costs for contracted personnel, instructions require combining associated wage-related costs with wages on contract labor lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 5 — Wage adjustment to common period using ECI
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust each hospital's total salaries plus wage-related costs to a common period using estimated percentage changes in the Employment Cost Index (ECI) for compensation for each 30-day increment from October 14, 2022 through April 15, 2024 for private industry hospital workers; factors are based on the midpoint of the cost reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ECI because it reflects total compensation (salaries plus fringe benefits) and includes managers and other hospital workers; methodology assures monthly update factors match actual quarterly and annual percent changes. CMS is not proposing changes to ECI usage for FY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 6 — Labor market area assignment prior to reclassifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign each hospital to its appropriate urban or rural labor market area before applying any reclassifications under section 1886(d)(8)(B), 1886(d)(8)(E), or 1886(d)(10) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment step occurs prior to any statutory reclassifications to ensure proper area wage comparisons.
